The University of Michigan updated its consumer sentiment index Friday with a preliminary August reading of 51, down about 8% from the final July index reading of 55.2.

The final August consumer sentiment index will be released on the 28th.

The school’s consumer sentiment tracker goes back decades and hit an all-time low in May. It had shown improvement across June and July before the downturn this month. [...] View PDF

The University of Michigan researchers collect nationwide surveys each month – asking people about business conditions, buying conditions, and personal finances – and use the feedback to calculate a consumer sentiment index.

results.title: Consumer sentiment falls in August as Americans 'just don't feel like they're thriving'

results.content: The University of Michigan released its preliminary Consumer Sentiment Index for August at 10am ET on Friday, and the number landed well below expectations. The reading came in at 51 — against a consensus forecast of 54.5 and a July final of 55.2. That is a decline of roughly 8% in a single month, reversing two consecutive months of improvement. The University of Michigan's Surveys of ​Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped ​to 51.0 this month from 55.2 in ⁠July, ending two straight months of improvement. ​Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index ​would be at 54.5.
